# Kruskal–Wallis test {.section}

Independent >2 samples

## Kruskal–Wallis test {.smaller .scrollable}

Created by [William Henry Kruskal](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kruskal) and [Wilson Allen Wallis](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Allen_Wallis), the Kruskal-Wallis test is a nonparametric alternative to the independent one-way ANOVA.

The Kruskal-Wallis test essentially subtracts the expected mean ranking from each observed mean ranking, which is $\chi^2$ distributed.

## Q-Q plot of the residuals {.smaller}

One-way ANOVA in JASP (as in the book, Figure 15.10)

```{r kw-qq-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5, fig.align='center'}
qqJasp(rstandard(lm(Testosterone ~ Soya, data = data)))
```

## Calculate H {.subsection}

$$H = \frac{12}{N(N+1)} \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{R_i^2}{n_i} - 3(N+1)$$

- $N$ total sample size
- $n_i$ sample size per group
- $k$ number of groups
- $R_i$ rank sums per group

## Calculate H

```{r kw-rank-sums, echo=TRUE}
# Now we need the sum of the ranks per group.
R.i <- aggregate(ranks ~ Soya, data = data, sum)$ranks
R.i

# De total sample size N is:
N <- nrow(data)

# And the sample size per group is n_i:
n.i <- aggregate(Testosterone ~ Soya, data=data, length)$Testosterone
n.i
```

## Calculate H {.smaller}

$$H = \frac{12}{N(N+1)} \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{R_i^2}{n_i} - 3(N+1)$$

```{r kw-h-statistic, echo=TRUE}
H <- ( 12/(N*(N+1)) ) * sum(R.i^2/n.i) - 3*(N+1)
H
```

And the degrees of freedom

```{r kw-h-p-value, echo=TRUE}
k  <- 4
df <- k - 1
```

## $\chi^2$ distribution {.smaller}

The $\chi^2$ distribution describes the test statistic under the assumption of $H_0$, given the degrees of freedom.

```{r kw-chisq-distribution, echo=FALSE}
#| output-location: slide

chi <- seq(0,8,.01)
df.plot <- c(1,2,3,6,8,10)
mycols  <- palette.colors(n = 7, palette = "Okabe-Ito")

plot( chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[1]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[1], type="l",
      main = "Chi squared distributions",
      ylab = "Density",
      ylim = c(0,1),
      xlab = "Chi squared")

lines(chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[2]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[2], type="l")
lines(chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[3]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[3], type="l")
lines(chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[4]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[4], type="l")
lines(chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[5]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[5], type="l")
lines(chi, dchisq(chi, df.plot[6]), lwd = 2, col = mycols[6], type="l")

legend("topright", legend = paste("df =",df.plot), col = mycols, lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

## Test for significance {.subsection}

```{r kw-test-for-significance, fig.align='center', warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
visualize_chisq_base(H = H, df = df, section = "upper")
```
